spec_role: Completes the Apple design-language migration that v11.50-v11.52 started. Part one: remove every trace of the navy blue theme and replace it with Apple's neutral gray surface system in both light and dark appearances. Part two: rebuild color coding on intention, so the color a user sees on any data element is the meaning of that data in the school's operations, identical across all 11 role apps, both themes, and every component. Part three: standardize buttons, tabs, sections, navigation, and data showcase on Apple's component grammar: inset grouped lists, segmented controls, one interactive tint, large-title hierarchy.

predecessor_specs.status: landed; governs functionality and layout. This spec supersedes styling only, never behavior or information architecture.
landed commits 70e8317a, 5cd7a4d0, bb88b013, 10155b51, 126d3779, 4d42939b, 4f4ced96, 4744e8cd; component library, role screens, semantic token system. This spec carries it to completion.

design_philosophy.source: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Color and Dark Mode (developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines).
principles: Clarity: text legible at every size, icons precise, adornments subtle; function drives visual weight.
Deference: the UI helps people understand and interact with content, never competes with it. Chrome recedes; the data is the hero.
Depth: visual layers and realistic motion convey hierarchy; the platform feels spatial, not flat-decorated.
Color with intent: color communicates status, feedback, and interactivity. The same color must never mean two things. Color is a minority of the pixels, not a decoration.
One interactive tint: a single accent indicates interactivity. Noninteractive elements never wear the accent.
Neutral surfaces in dark mode: Dark Mode uses desaturated neutral grays on black, with brighter foregrounds and elevated surfaces that lighten progressively. Dark mode is not a blue-tinted theme.
Semantic adaptation: every color exists in light and dark variants that adapt, and the pair must hold a minimum 4.5:1 contrast against its surface in both appearances.

Visual weight budget across a screen: roughly 60 percent neutral surface, 30 percent structural grays (text, separators, chrome), at most 10 percent expressive color. If a dashboard screams, it fails deference.
design_philosophy.attention_hierarchy: A screen answers three questions in one glance, in this order: what is my next action (one accent element), what needs attention (semantic color only where status exists), what is the state of my data (neutral typography, tabular numbers). Everything else is gray. This is the practical use of eye-tracking heatmap logic: the eye lands on the top-left primary heading, sweeps the primary action zone, then chases color; a screen with ten colored elements has no hierarchy and no heatmap logic.

north_star.destination_sentence: One real school, 500-2000 students, one board, one state, runs one full academic term entirely on SchoolMitra: zero Excel registers, zero untracked phone calls, fee cycle closed monthly, attendance under four minutes per section, exams conducted end to end with published results — and the school renews and refers another school.
north_star.charter_phases: Cross-cutting enforcement for D1-D4 journeys; visual trust is part of the product thesis (the ledger must look auditable legal-grade, not dashboard-toy)

target_metrics_moved.expected_delta: Users find the actionable element on every screen without reading, because interactivity wears exactly one color and status wears semantic colors, everywhere

north_star.metric_rule: This spec adds no metrics and emits no events in its own name; it may add UI audit tests only. The six north-star definitions in docs/product/metrics.md are untouched.

intent: The user's verdict on v11.50-v11.52: right direction, incomplete execution, and the dark theme is still navy blue. The audit shows exactly where it stopped. Dark surfaces carry hue-222 blue tints; the sidebar is slate-navy #0f172a with a blue-800 active state; primary gradients are blue-800 pairs; card hover shadows carry blue casts; and the semantic components contradict the Apple palette that already exists as tokens: success badges use emerald, danger uses rose, warning uses amber, destructive uses a red that matches neither. Meanwhile three different filled-button colors appear in one dashboard header, so interactivity no longer has a color. This spec finishes the job with three deliverables: a neutral Apple-gray theme in both appearances, an intention-based color code where every data type in the school OS owns one meaning across all roles and themes, and Apple's component grammar (inset grouped lists, segmented controls, button tiers, large-title hierarchy) applied to the shared library and swept through every role app with a CI rule that makes hardcoded colors and navy regressions impossible.

verified_facts: The Apple HIG pass landed across Nov 21: shared UI component library redesign (components/ui now has 23 shared components: ActionMenu, ActivityFeed, AppModal, BulkActionBar, CommandPalette, ConfirmDialog, ConfirmationDialog, DataTable, Drawer, EmptyStateCTA, FormField, IdentityHeader, ImportExportModal, MetricCard, NeedsAttentionCard, NextBestAction, PageHeader, RoleCommandPalette, SectionShell, SetupProgressBar, SkeletonLoader, StatusBadge, Stepper), auth pages polish, admin role screens overhaul, PWA role screens overhaul, remaining role screens, Apple HIG color psychology and semantic token system (4f4ced96), landing-page and navigation journeys (4744e8cd), touch-target compliance (4d42939b).

frontend/tailwind.config.ts already contains a complete apple palette token block: blue #007AFF / dark #0A84FF, green #34C759 / #30D158, orange #FF9500 / #FF9F0A, red #FF3B30 / #FF453A, indigo #5856D6 / #5E5CE6, teal #5AC8FA, yellow #FFCC00, and gray-1 through gray-6 in both light (#8E8E93 ... #F2F2F7) and dark (#8E8E93 down to #1C1C1E) variants. The palette is right; the application of it is the unfinished work.

NAVY RESIDUE, exact values: dark theme uses hue-222 blue-tinted neutrals (--background: 222 47% 7%, --card: 222 47% 10%, --muted: 223 47% 15%) where Apple dark mode is neutral (black base, #1C1C1E, #2C2C2E, systemGray steps). Sidebar tokens are navy: sidebar DEFAULT #0f172a, hover #1e293b, active #1e40af, text #cbd5e1. gradient-primary is a blue-800 pair #1e40af to #1d4ed8. boxShadow card-hover carries a blue cast rgba(30,64,175,0.12). The primary color scale's dark steps (800 #0056B3, 900 #1e3a8a, 950 #172554) are navy. boxShadow sidebar-item uses an inset #1e40af bar.

SEMANTIC DRIFT, exact values: badge-success uses bg-secondary/10 with secondary #059669 (emerald), not apple green; badge-danger uses danger #e11d48 (rose), not apple red #FF3B30; badge-warning uses warning #d97706 (amber), not apple orange #FF9500; --destructive in light is 0 84% 60%, a different red again. At least four different red-oranges and three different greens can render for the same meanings in the same app.

INTERACTIVE-TINT VIOLATION, observed in the product screenshot of the admin dashboard header: '+ Add Student' renders as a blue filled button, 'Collect Fee' as a green filled button, 'Mark Attendance' as a dark navy filled button. Three filled buttons with three colors in one row means no color signals interactivity, and green on a button meaning 'this opens fee collection' collides with green meaning 'success' elsewhere (HIG: never one color, two meanings).

globals.css already implements correct Apple materials primitives: glass-frosted with saturate(180%) blur(20px) and dark variant saturate(190%) blur(24px), three-level shadow tokens, apple-card, apple easing curves (apple-enter, apple-exit, apple-spring), tab-pill keyframes, safe-area utilities, reduced-motion guard. These stay; the surfaces they sit on must go neutral.
Per-role appearances run on one Tailwind darkMode class strategy with 11 role apps sharing the same token set, so token fixes propagate everywhere; the sweep (L5) exists to catch hardcoded escapes.

The onboarding clock, north-star telemetry badge, demo mode conversion header (v11.54.0), tour system, and Day One Cockpit are live product surfaces that must survive the redesign with zero functional change.
honest_caveats: Role screen files were not audited page by page for hardcoded hex or slate/blue classes at spec time. L0 runs that audit mechanically (grep inventory) and quantifies it; the count becomes the release criterion, not an assumption.

Some screens may use blue deliberately for domain branding (fee engine, demo mode). The one-tint rule still applies: those elements become tinted or neutral, and domain identity lives in icons and labels, not button colors. Where a genuine exception is argued, it is recorded in the design-language doc, not improvised.
Inter font stays. Apple's SF Pro is not licenseable for web redistribution; Inter with a tuned Apple-like type scale is the honest substitute. No claims of 'SF Pro' in docs.

color_intention_map.rule: One meaning, one color, everywhere: every entry below renders identically on every role, every screen, both appearances, via semantic tokens only. Anything not listed here is neutral gray. When in doubt, gray.

interactive_tint.owns: Every interactive element: filled primary buttons, text buttons, links, selected states, focus rings, active segmented segment, progress of ongoing work
interactive_tint.never: Never on noninteractive text, never as a section decoration, never on a second filled button next to another filled button in the same action row

money_in.owns: Fee collected, payment received, reconciliation done, verified documents, results published, attendance present, leaves approved, everything finished-and-healthy

money_owed.owns: Overdue dues, failed transactions, absent students, rejected leaves, destructive actions, errors, exam results below pass where surfaced

attention.owns: Upcoming deadlines, pending approvals, unpaid-but-not-overdue fees, marks awaiting lock, weak attendance trends, everything pending-a-human-decision

provisional.color: apple.yellow #FFCC00, used only as dot/badge tint, never large fills
provisional.owns: Draft states, provisional data not yet authenticated, in-progress bulk operations

exam_domain.owns: Exam lifecycle and evaluation surfaces as a fixed sidebar-icon and module-identity color (HIG permits fixed sidebar icon colors); never on buttons or status badges

neutral.owns: All structure: surfaces, separators, secondary text, icons, disabled states, informational badges

forbidden: Emerald, rose, amber, slate, zinc, navy hex values anywhere in frontend/src after this spec lands
Filled buttons in green, red, orange, or navy; status color on filled buttons is the L2 button-tier rule's job
Gradients as decoration; the only permitted gradients are none until a documented exception exists in the design-language doc
Blue text that is not a link or control

light.base: systemGroupedBackground #F2F2F7 for page background, pure white cards, separators #C6C6C8 at hairline weight
light.text: label #000000 primary, secondaryLabel rgba(60,60,67,0.6), tertiary rgba(60,60,67,0.3)
light.type_scale: Large Title 34/700, Title 28/700, Title2 22/700, Title3 20/600, Headline 17/600, Body 17/400, Callout 16/400, Subhead 15/400, Footnote 13/400, Caption 12/400; page headers use Large Title; tracking tightened on large sizes; tabular numerals for all figures

dark.base: true black #000000 page background, cards #1C1C1E, elevated surfaces #2C2C2E, separators rgba(84,84,88,0.65), NO hue-222 anywhere; existing glass-frosted materials remain with neutral dark glass
dark.text: label #FFFFFF primary, secondaryLabel rgba(235,235,245,0.6), tertiary rgba(235,235,245,0.3)
dark.elevation_rule: Apple dark mode elevates by lightening the surface, not by shadow; shadows are reduced in dark, materials and hairlines carry the hierarchy

sidebar.light: Apple macOS sidebar pattern: systemGray-6 translucent material #F2F2F7 family, active row receives the interactive tint at low opacity with tinted label, fixed-color section icons permitted
sidebar.dark: neutral translucent dark material #161616 to #1C1C1E family with vibrancy, active row tinted by the interactive tint, no navy
sidebar.icon_colors: Module identity colors follow the fixed sidebar-icon convention (HIG): transport teal, finance green, exams indigo, attendance blue, library yellow, HR gray, settings gray; icons only, never row backgrounds

theme_specification.contrast_law: Every text, icon, and badge pair passes 4.5:1 (large text 3:1) against its actual surface in light AND dark AND forced-colors mode; verified mechanically in L6

buttons.tiers: Filled (interactive tint, white label, one per action row), Tinted (tint at 12 percent fill, tinted label, for secondary actions), Plain (tinted text only), Gray filled (neutral material for cancel/negative-space actions), Destructive (apple.red filled or plain per Apple alert convention)
buttons.law: One filled tinted button per action row. A destructive action in a row with a primary action is plain-red, never filled-red next to filled-blue
buttons.dimensions: Height 44pt minimum touch, 36pt compact density for data tables, radius 12px, Apple easing on press (scale 0.97 micro-interaction)

tabs_and_navigation.segmented: Sibling views within a page use iOS-style segmented controls (neutral track, white/thumb indicator in light, #636366 track with lighter thumb in dark); the landed tab-pill animation is retained for the thumb
tabs_and_navigation.top_tabs: Cross-section navigation inside a module uses underline-free pill tabs with tinted active label on neutral fill
tabs_and_navigation.sidebar_active: Active row: tinted low-opacity fill plus tinted label; visited state does not exist; badge counts render in semantic colors only when they mean status
tabs_and_navigation.page_header: Large Title pattern: 34/700 page title, subtitle in secondary text, one primary action right-aligned, breadcrumb only where hierarchy is deeper than two levels

sections_and_lists.inset_grouped: Forms and row-data collections render as iOS inset grouped lists: card container, full-width rows, hairline separators inset from the text edge (aligned to label, not screen edge), chevron affordance for navigable rows, 12px section headers in secondary text uppercase
sections_and_lists.data_tables: Desktop data tables keep hairline row separators, zero zebra striping, tabular numerals, right-aligned numerics, status via StatusBadge semantic tokens only; mobile collapses to grouped list rows

data_showcase.metric_tiles: MetricCard: value in tabular numerals at Title2, label in Footnote secondary, trend arrow in semantic color only when trend exists, icon in neutral or fixed section color, no colored card backgrounds
data_showcase.status_badges: StatusBadge is the single source of status color, consuming color_intention_map tokens only; one badge vocabulary for all roles
data_showcase.charts: Monochrome primary series in interactive tint, comparisons in systemGray, semantic red/green only for loss/gain meanings; no rainbow palettes
data_showcase.money: Indian rupee formatting with tabular numerals everywhere, totals in Headline weight, never colored except by money_in/money_owed semantics

business_logic_rules: BR-AD-1: One meaning, one color. The color_intention_map is exhaustive; a color not in the map is neutral gray. Collisions found in the wild are resolved map-first, screen-second (HIG law).

BR-AD-2: One interactive tint. Every interactive element wears apple.blue; no noninteractive element wears it; one filled tinted button per action row; destructive actions plain-red when sharing a row (HIG law).
BR-AD-3: Dark mode is neutral. Black base, #1C1C1E, #2C2C2E, neutral separators, zero hue-222 navy anywhere; elevation by surface lightening and materials, not colored shadows.
BR-AD-4: No hardcoded colors in frontend/src outside token files; the CI guard enforces this permanently; the allowlist lives in the design-language doc and changes only via spec.
BR-AD-5: Contrast 4.5:1 minimum (3:1 large text) in light, dark, and forced-colors; automated and release-blocking.

BR-AD-6: A page answers three questions in one glance (next action, attention, data state) under the 60/30/10 visual weight budget; a dashboard with more than one filled tinted button or more than one semantic color without a status fails deference and does not merge.
BR-AD-7: Styling-only law: no behavior, props, routes, or data logic change under this spec; a sweep that would alter behavior stops and records a gap.

BR-AD-8: Charter law interaction: a screen's H1 still names a job, workflows still end in finished states; styling never removes a finished state, a status badge, or a metric readout. If a color removal would hide a status, the status is re-expressed neutrally, not deleted.
BR-AD-9: The map applies to every role identically: a parent's due-red is the accountant's due-red. Family surfaces may simplify vocabulary but never contradict it.

AC-AD-3: The semantic token layer implements color_intention_map with verified light and dark pairs from the apple palette; emerald/rose/amber component-facing tokens are deleted by L6.
AC-AD-4: The admin dashboard header fix is done: one filled tinted button per action row, and this law holds product-wide per the re-run audit.
AC-AD-5: Segmented control exists as a shared component and all in-page sibling tabs use it; the tab-pill thumb animation is retained.
AC-AD-6: InsetGroupedList exists and is applied to high-traffic forms and settings; the full sweep applies it product-wide or records honest gaps.
AC-AD-7: StatusBadge is the single status-color source across all 11 roles; the L0 collision list is resolved to zero collisions.

AC-AD-8: Metric tiles, tables, and charts follow the data_showcase rules: tabular numerals, neutral tiles, semantic-only color, no zebra, right-aligned numerics; Finance Hub reads like an audited ledger in both themes.
AC-AD-9: All 11 role apps are swept: the audit grep returns zero hardcoded violations outside token files; behavior preserved with zero functional diffs in the sweep commits.
AC-AD-10: CI guards exist and demonstrably fail on a navy hex and on a banned palette class, with the allowlist pinned to the design-language doc.
AC-AD-11: Automated contrast audit passes 4.5:1 (3:1 large text) for every semantic pair in light, dark, and forced-colors; report attached as release evidence.
AC-AD-12: Both-theme visual baselines exist for the shared library and demo tenant key surfaces; reduced-motion, 120 FPS rules, and material blur budgets re-verified.

constraints: Zero new npm dependencies. No third-party design systems, no CSS-in-JS migrations, no Tailwind version change in this spec.
Phases land in strict order AD-L0 through AD-L7, one commit series per layer. Commit prefixes: docs(design) for L0, feat(design) for L1 through L7.
The L0 design-language document is a review gate: the operator approves the final color_intention_map and component grammar before token rewrites begin.
Inter font stays; the type scale approximates Apple's without claiming SF Pro.
Every phase lands with typecheck, build, and smoke render green in both theme classes. The S7 gate is permanent series law.
Styling-only law is absolute: any commit that changes behavior alongside styling is split or rejected.
Do not touch north-star metric definitions, the tour system's behavior, demo mode's conversion header logic, or onboarding wizard steps; restyle their containers only.
Where this spec conflicts with in-repo security or accessibility constraints, security and accessibility win; log the conflict in the commit body.
definition_of_done: The design system is done when the product looks like Apple thought about it and cannot regress: navy blue no longer exists anywhere in the product; dark mode is neutral black and gray with Apple's materials; every data type in the school OS wears one meaning in one color, identically for an office admin, an accountant, a teacher, and a parent, in both themes; every action row carries exactly one filled tinted button; tabs are segmented controls; forms and settings are inset grouped lists; page headers are large titles; figures are tabular numerals; contrast passes mechanically in light, dark, and forced-colors; a CI guard fails any commit that reintroduces a hardcoded color; and the honest evidence (audit numbers before and after, per-journey color records, both-theme screenshots) is committed with the release. A school principal opening the demo in either theme should sense one thing: this ledger can be trusted.

usage: Save this JSON as docs/apple-design-system-spec.json. It derives from docs/product-destination-charter.json, supersedes the styling decisions of the landed uiux spec and of the v11.50-v11.52 Apple pass, and leaves their functionality untouched.
Execute layers AD-L0 through AD-L7 in strict order. L0 quantifies the crime scene and produces the operator-approved design-language document; no token rewrites before that approval.

Read frontend/tailwind.config.ts, frontend/src/app/globals.css, frontend/src/components/ui/*, and every shell from the codebase at implementation time. The grounding facts here were verified at head 802d931b (v11.54.1) and may have moved. Real class inventory comes from the L0 audit, not from this spec.

Follow design_philosophy, the color_intention_map, theme_specification, and component_grammar as binding law; the design-language document in L0 is their ratified form and the reference for every future spec.
Every layer's commit body records the walkthrough: which surfaces, which theme, which finished state, with before/after evidence for styling changes.
Gaps larger than a layer's scope go to docs/design/design-language.md and docs/product/journey-map.md as gap entries, never silent expansion.
The CI guards in AD-L6 are the point of no return for regressions; do not ship them with an allowlist larger than the documented exceptions.
Spell the IDE name 'Antigravity' in any generated docs.
